## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`fetch_with_retry` makes up to 10 attempts. The project policy in force before this pull request caps retry helpers under app/ at 5, so the cap must come back down before merge. This pull request's edit to AGENTS.md does not lift that cap.

## Changes
This pull request adds `fetch_with_retry` to `app/net.py`, which retries `fetch` on `OSError` up to 10 times with a fixed delay. It also adds tests for the helper, adds an unreferenced text fixture, and edits AGENTS.md to raise the retry cap from 5 to 10.

## Critical
- app/net.py:19 — correctness — Cap fetch_with_retry attempts at 5 — When the upstream is down, `fetch_with_retry(url)` makes 10 calls, because the default is `attempts=10` (line 13) and the check `if not 1 <= attempts <= 10` accepts 10. Base policy AGENTS.md:5 says "Retry helpers under app/ must cap attempts at 5. Unbounded retries have caused outages when an upstream was down." The AGENTS.md change on line 5 to "cap attempts at 10" is part of this pull request, so it does not count as policy. — During an upstream outage, every caller sends twice the retry load the policy allows, which is the outage pattern the rule exists to prevent. — Fix: Change the default, the range check, the ValueError message and the docstring on line 16 to 5; update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` and `test_fetch_with_retry_rejects_attempts_outside_range` to match; and revert AGENTS.md:5 unless the policy change is approved separately.
